**NextGenOS Setup Studio**, version {{VERSION}}, part of the Smart Retail AI Ecosystem by NextGenOS. **For NextGenOS staff only: never give it to a customer.** Proprietary software: see `EULA.txt`.

**What it is.** The program your team uses to set up a new customer. A person opens it, starts a new project for a new company, fills in the company's details (name, country, kind of business, look, words, first items), and the Studio puts together the customer's setup for them. It holds no licence keys and no source code, and it sells nothing: a customer's licence key comes from the NextGenOS Licence Studio.

### Read this before you test

- **What the Studio needs to make a customer's setup.** It does not build the shop program, the website or the Android app: it puts them together from the files of a full release, which carry the licence keys. Programs from a trial release (no licence keys) can only make a pack marked as a trial, and the Studio refuses to make a customer's pack from them.
- **The website and the Android app.** Their settings are built into them, so each customer's website and app is built for that customer on GitHub, not on the Studio's PC. The customer's pack says how.
- **Test build.** A person has not yet run this on a real Windows PC with eyes on it (the release workflow opens it on a Windows runner and checks that it starts, answers, shows its window, runs once and quits). The black-window flash some programs show for a moment has not been looked for by a person.
- **Not signed.** Windows will say "Windows protected your PC" until the program is signed with NextGenOS's certificate: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
- **Tax.** Each country's rates and invoice wording are data, not legal advice. A local tax adviser must check them before a shop uses them.
- **Source code protection** makes the programs costly to read; it cannot make code on a PC impossible to read.
